title: Kernel handshake weekly log - Mar 29 2026
content:
Purpose and scope:
Quick weekly field log capturing work on the kernel handshake protocol, observed latency degradations during handshake failure modes, KV handoff experiments, and next actions. This is a working note — trying to capture traces, small repro steps, and discussion points for the larger postmortem sketch.

Summary (TL;DR):
- We saw a ~15-40ms tail latency increase on 99p for short-sequence chat requests during a handshake regression introduced by staggered kernel upgrades on Mar 28.
- Root cause sketch: mismatch in async handshake backoff + KV-cache state reconciliation path caused repeated lightweight kernel restarts and microretries that broke batching affinity for a subset of clients (mostly those on non-primary routing).
- Quick mitigation applied: reverted handshake backoff change in stable branch and enabled conservative affinity hold (30s) for routes affected. Metrics stabilized in ~90m.
- Ongoing: repro harness for cross-kernel handshake, small kernel-side lock removal experiment, and longer-term: explicit handshake version negotiation + opaque session tickets.

What happened (timeline):
- 2026-03-28 09:45 UTC: rolling deploy of kernel v0.26.3 (contains handshake backoff change: exponential->adaptive) started across cluster. No traffic shaping.
- 2026-03-28 10:07 UTC: Canary region reported 99p latency up from 210ms -> 260ms on short (<=64 token) sequences. Alerts triggered.
- 2026-03-28 10:12 UTC: Debug traces show repeated handshake attempts between serving-agent and kernel (3-6 attempts per request) for ~2% of requests. These requests then missed batching windows and fell back to single-request execution path.
- 2026-03-28 10:35 UTC: Reverted handshake backoff change (rollback to exponential) on stable. Enabled short-term affinity hold=30s for impacted routes.
- 2026-03-28 11:50 UTC: Latency metrics returned near baseline.

Key observations from traces and logs:
- Failure mode pattern: lightweight handshake failure (no full disconnect) where kernel returned ACCEPT but with transient KV version mismatch header. Serving agent responded by starting handshake retry logic rather than continuing with existing session. This produced microretries but left the request in non-batched path.
- Affected requests heavily skewed to multi-tenant routing path B (short sequences, high qps, lower priority). Primary routing path A (reserved/dedicated) saw <0.2% impact.
- KV mismatch header was set by kernels that had applied an async prefetch optimization (kvcache prefill v2) which writes a provisional version until secondary commit finishes. If the agent saw provisional+late-commit, current handshake logic considered it mismatch and retried.
- Batch affinity: when handshake retried, serving-agent releases batching slot immediately; retries land on next available kernel which often had different batch composition resulting in single-request execution.

Experiments run this week (notes + quick data):
1) Local repro: synthetic client with handshake thrash enabled
   - Setup: 50 clients, 200 rps, sequence len 24, random routing to both kernel variants.
   - Result: reproduced 12-18ms p99 tail increase when provisional-kv path toggled on.

2) Affinity hold experiment (short-term mitigation)
   - Enabled affinity hold for 30s on 10% of routes.
   - Effect: reduced p99 increase by ~60% for those routes. Reduced overall microretries by half.

3) Kernel-side lock removal patch (local only)
   - Attempt: reduce time window where provisional version is visible by moving commit to a faster code path.
   - Result: lowered observed provisional window but did not fully remove handshake mismatch in synthetic test. Needs more unit testing.

Open hypotheses to validate:
- Hypothesis A: Handshake backoff logic switch to adaptive increased the chance that a transient provisional header is seen and triggers retry, because retries were attempted faster (before commit finished) and thus more likely to observe provisional state.
- Hypothesis B: Agent-side logic is too conservative: any version mismatch triggers a full handshake retry; we can be safe to accept provisional->commit within the same request if there is no other error.
- Hypothesis C: When retries happen, current batching window implementation treats them as cold requests; a small change to keep slot until commit would preserve batching.

Short-term action items (owner & ETA):
- Aisha: publish mini postmortem + update incident ticket SRV-1357 (ETA 2026-04-02).
- Diego: add stronger logging on KV provisional headers and handshake attempt counts, deploy to canary (ETA 2026-04-01).
- Maya: complete and run the cross-kernel repro harness (GHPR #842) with both kernels and provisional commit toggles (ETA 2026-04-05).
- Ethan: draft agent change to tolerate provisional->commit within same request and run unit tests (ETA 2026-04-09).
- SRE: schedule blue/green for next kernel rollout and include traffic shaping (ETA ops ticket SRV-1360).

Longer-term design proposals to consider:
- Session tickets: create opaque session ticket that binds serving-agent to kernel-session for N seconds, so transient provisional state won’t force handshake semantics per-request.
- Handshake version negotiation: include explicit handshake version and capability flags. If kernel advertises provisional-commit optimization, agent should follow a backcompat path.
- Batching resilience: on retry, allow agent to request same batch slot if the same kernel is reachable within X ms; or create ephemeral requeue slot with batching priority preserved.

Repro steps (for engineers wanting to reproduce locally):
1) Checkout PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
2) Start two kernels: v0.26.2 (stable) and v0.26.3 (handshake-adaptive).
3) Run synthetic client harness: scripts/handshake_harness/run.sh --clients 50 --rps 200 --seq 24 --provisional-toggle on
4) Watch /metrics and traces on localhost:9411 for handshake.attempts and kvcache.provisional_window_ms

Questions for the wider team / points for review: 
- Are we comfortable with aggressive rollback during rollouts until we have explicit session tickets? (ops, SRE)
- Do we accept a short-term agent tweak to be permissive of provisional states? Is this a correctness risk? (serving runtime + research)
- Should model-specific slow-commit patterns be surfaced by the model onboarding process (so we don’t surprise runtime with provisional writes)? (applied-ml + model-onboarding)

Appendix: useful snippets from trace logs (redacted)
- trace-id: 0f2b...: handshake attempt 1 -> kernel v0.26.3 (ACCEPT, kv-version: provisional:432) -> agent starts retry -> attempt 2 -> kernel v0.26.3 (ACCEPT, kv-version: committed:433) -> request executed single-request path.
- metric snapshot (10:00-11:00 UTC): p50 48ms, p95 160ms, p99 270ms (peak at 10:20). Reversion baseline p99 ~230ms.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this log short and focused; avoid full incident writeup here. Consolidate into SRV-1357 for exec-read.
- Remember to notify product about possible customer-facing blips; CS already received one ping from a customer on routing B.

If you find other traces or can repro differently, drop them in this doc or link GH PR with harness results. Will sync in next serving-runtime weekly on Mon.

— Aisha
